digest.headline: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max and Meta's Muse Code headline a crowded model week, Anthropic names its first policy chief, and the White House quietly locks in a voluntary AI safety framework
digest.summary: Alibaba unveiled Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4T-parameter MoE model scoring 58 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index and closing in on Western frontier labs, with open weights due within the week. Two days later Meta shipped Muse Code, a terminal coding agent built on the new Muse Spark 1.2 model, and Liquid AI released LFM2.5-2.6B, an on-device agentic model that runs agent loops on phones and even a Raspberry Pi. On the policy side, Anthropic hired former California Supreme Court Justice Tino Cuéllar as its first Chief Global Affairs Officer the same week a dozen AI companies met the White House to finalize a voluntary frontier-model evaluation framework that won't be made public. All three major coding harnesses shipped again: Claude Code patched a Bash permission-bypass vulnerability and added self-hosted runners, Codex CLI added portable Agent Plugins, and Pi shipped a fullscreen TUI mode.

stories.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Max, a 2.4T-parameter MoE model closing in on Western frontier labs
stories.dek: Qwen3.8-Max activates 95B of its 2.4 trillion parameters per token, handles text, image, and video up to a million tokens of context, and scored 58 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index — up from 46 for Qwen3.7-Max and now ahead of every US lab except Anthropic and OpenAI on that measure. It's live on Alibaba Cloud's Model Studio now, with open weights due within the week, making it the first Max-class Qwen model to be open-sourced.
stories.whyItMatters: A trillion-parameter-class model from a Chinese lab landing within a few points of Claude Fable 5 on a public benchmark — and shipping open weights days later — keeps narrowing the gap between closed frontier labs and open alternatives that anyone can self-host.

stories.title: Meta enters the coding-agent race with Muse Code, built on new Muse Spark 1.2 model
stories.dek: Muse Code is Meta's first terminal coding agent: a replay-exact, restart-safe event log, approval-gated /plan and stress-testing /grill skills, and background agents that persist for a whole session instead of spawning per task. It runs on Muse Spark 1.2, which scored 54–57 on Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index (xhigh) and 82.9% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 under Meta's own harness — behind Claude Opus 5's 86.7% but ahead of Codex and Grok Build's scores on the same test. Pricing is $1.25/$4.25 per million input/output tokens.
stories.whyItMatters: Meta is now fielding a full coding-agent stack — model plus terminal harness — rather than just an API model, putting it in direct competition with Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor rather than just their underlying models; note the headline benchmark numbers are Meta's own harness, not independently reproduced.

stories.title: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-2.6B runs full agent loops entirely on-device, no cloud required
stories.dek: LFM2.5-2.6B is a 2.6B dense model with a 128K context window and native tool calling, built to plan and run multi-step agentic tasks locally on phones, laptops, and even a Raspberry Pi. It hits 220 tokens/sec on an Apple M5 Max in under 2.5GB of memory, ships day-zero support for llama.cpp, MLX, vLLM, SGLang, and ONNX, and is trained to work inside agent harnesses including Pi. Weights are open on Hugging Face.
stories.whyItMatters: A sub-3B model that leads larger models on tool-use and instruction-following benchmarks while running fully offline pushes agentic AI toward zero-marginal-cost, private, on-device deployment — relevant for anyone building agents that shouldn't depend on a live API connection.

stories.title: Anthropic names Tino Cuéllar its first Chief Global Affairs Officer
stories.dek: Mariano-Florentino "Tino" Cuéllar — a former California Supreme Court justice and outgoing president of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace — will lead Anthropic's policy, international engagement, and government relations, reporting to President Daniela Amodei. He arrives as Anthropic contests a Pentagon blacklist and Fable 5 export controls and prepares for a potential IPO.
stories.whyItMatters: Creating a dedicated C-suite policy role signals Anthropic expects sustained, high-stakes government friction rather than a one-off dispute — worth tracking for anyone whose Claude usage touches regulated industries or government contracts.

stories.title: White House finalizes voluntary AI evaluation framework with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta — details stay classified
stories.dek: About a dozen companies, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft, and Nvidia, met White House officials to close out a voluntary framework — stemming from a June executive order — under which companies can give the government early access to frontier models for up to 30 days. The administration confirmed the framework won't be publicly released and much of its content will be classified; it explicitly cannot be used to create a mandatory licensing regime.
stories.whyItMatters: A US federal AI safety framework is now locked in without public disclosure of its actual standards — a notable contrast with the EU's published, enforceable AI Act transparency rules that took effect five days earlier.

stories.title: ByteDance launches SeedRealtime, a full-duplex model that watches, listens, and speaks at once
stories.dek: SeedRealtime natively fuses continuous audio, video, and text streams in one end-to-end model rather than stitching together separate ASR, vision, and TTS components. It decides conversational timing itself — tracking scenes, speakers, and pauses to judge when to answer — and can speak unprompted when it spots a requested object or an on-screen mistake. It's now fully rolled out inside the Douyin app.
stories.whyItMatters: Full-duplex, always-watching multimodal models at consumer scale (rather than as a research demo) push voice/video assistants toward genuinely continuous interaction instead of turn-based request-response.

stories.title: Claude Code patches a Bash permission-check bypass in v2.1.223
stories.dek: Claude Code 2.1.223 fixed a vulnerability where crafted commands — including ones padded with tabs or invisible Unicode — could hide part of themselves from Bash permission checks and approval-dialog review. The same release fixed a gap where an agent definition's bypassPermissions mode ignored an org's bypass-permissions-disable policy, and closed a sandbox escape via dynamic import() in workflow scripts.
stories.whyItMatters: If you rely on Claude Code's permission prompts or org-level bypass policies as a safety boundary for autonomous runs, this is a real gap that's now closed — worth updating rather than treating as routine changelog noise.

modelsMeta.note: Best score per column is highlighted. Qwen3.8-Max and Muse Spark 1.2 are this week's new entrants — Qwen3.8-Max at 58.0 on the AA index (a 2.4T-parameter MoE model, open weights pending) and Muse Spark 1.2 at 57.0, powering Meta's new Muse Code agent. Neither has a published score yet on epoch.ai's CursorBench or Datacurve's DeepSWE leaderboard. Claude Opus 5 still leads the index outright at 61.0.

harness.notes: Adds self-hosted environments via `claude self-hosted-runner` (Team/Enterprise), an `archive` plugin source for installing plugins from a zip over HTTPS without git or npm, and cross-session messaging (SendMessage/ListAgents). Follows 2.1.223, which fixed a Bash permission-check bypass exploitable with tab- or Unicode-padded commands and a sandbox escape via dynamic import() in workflow scripts.

Adds portable Agent Plugins with search across local, personal, workspace, and remote catalogs, persistent thread sections with manual ordering, an `--approve-for-me` auto-approval flag, Cursor skill migration with synchronized imports from Claude conversations, and support for the MCP 2026-07-28 spec's paginated discovery.

Adds a fullscreen TUI mode with a sticky editor and independently scrollable transcript, Mermaid diagram and LaTeX rendering, and directory-specific context overrides via AGENTS.override.md. Includes breaking API changes: renamed interfaces (ModelsRequestTransforms), reworked message_update event emissions, and a v4 lane-based session model.

extensions.name: Agent Plugins
extensions.blurb: Portable plugin manifests you can search across local, personal, workspace, and remote catalogs, plus workspace-level plugin publishing — shipped in Codex 0.147.0.

extensions.name: Archive plugin source
extensions.blurb: Install Claude Code plugins straight from a zip file over HTTPS — no git or npm required — with optional SHA-256 pinning for supply-chain integrity.

extensions.name: pi-claude-marketplace
extensions.blurb: Lets Pi Coding Agent install commands, skills, agents, hooks, and MCP servers straight from Claude Code plugin marketplaces — bootstrap the official Anthropic marketplace and install with the same UX as Claude Code's /plugin.

tips.title: Point at a reference file instead of describing your conventions
tips.body: Rather than explaining your coding style or conventions in prose, name or @-reference a file that already embodies them — "follow the patterns in components/Button.tsx" — and let the agent read the source directly. Anthropic's own prompt-engineering guidance calls this out as more reliable than verbal description, and it applies to any convention-following task, not just code style.

tips.title: Use task dependencies (blockedBy) instead of hoping parallel agents don't collide
tips.body: When breaking a large refactor into many pieces, mark tasks with blockedBy relationships to form a dependency graph rather than just firing off sub-agents in parallel — Claude Code auto-unblocks dependent tasks as prerequisites finish, and workers claim tasks via ownership tracking, which avoids the conflicts that come from multiple agents editing without any ordering.

tips.title: Give monorepo subdirectories their own agent instructions with AGENTS.override.md
tips.body: Pi 0.84 added directory-specific context overrides: drop an AGENTS.override.md in a subdirectory and the agent picks up different rules there than at the repo root — useful for monorepos where a frontend package and a backend service genuinely need different conventions instead of one bloated top-level instructions file.
